notes: quality = LLMRouterBench per-item score as published (task-specific grader)
cost = LLMRouterBench realised per-call USD for the *measured* model
tokens_in / tokens_out = MEASURED token counts, not derived from text length
items keyed by sha1(dataset, normalised prompt); 25,035 kept
PROXY-BACKED: quality and tokens are measured on a stand-in model per slot, not on the Chutes endpoint. See catalog.CHUTES_PROXY for each binding.
cost = measured tokens x published Chutes price (the proxy's own bill is discarded)
2037 zero-token, zero-score cells marked unobserved as failed calls

bindings.label: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B
bindings.why: Same family and size class — NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano line, small and non-thinking.

bindings.label: Mistral Nemo Instruct
bindings.why: No Mistral checkpoint is graded anywhere in the corpus. The closest measured analogue is a small non-thinking general instruct model of the same generation.

bindings.label: DeepSeek V4 Flash
bindings.why: DeepSeek family, small 'flash' class, reasoning-capable — matching the catalogue entry's thinks=True at the cheap end of the pool.

bindings.label: Gemma 4 31B Turbo
bindings.why: Gemma family; the only Google open-weights model the corpus grades.

bindings.label: Qwen3 32B
bindings.why: Qwen3 generation, dense open model — same line, one size class down.

bindings.label: Qwen3 235B Thinking
bindings.why: The identical checkpoint. The catalogue id and the measured id name the same weights, so this column is not a proxy at all.

bindings.label: DeepSeek V3.2
bindings.why: DeepSeek V3 line, adjacent point release.

bindings.label: Qwen3.6 27B
bindings.why: WEAKEST BINDING IN THE TABLE. No Qwen checkpoint is left unassigned at this capability, so this slot is matched on measured capability and mid-tier price alone. The family is wrong and the 'code and analysis' speciality is not reproduced; treat this column's per-task profile as the least trustworthy.

bindings.label: Qwen3.5 397B
bindings.why: Qwen large MoE, non-thinking — same architecture class as the catalogue entry.

bindings.label: GLM 5.1
bindings.why: GLM family, the strongest GLM checkpoint the corpus grades.

bindings.label: Kimi K2.6
bindings.why: Kimi K2 line — the catalogue entry is a later point release of these weights.

bindings.label: GLM 5.2
bindings.why: Family unmatched, and deliberately so. A frontier slot needs a column that beats every mid-tier model, and glm-4.6 — already bound to GLM 5.1 — is the only GLM measured and does not clear that bar. Capability-matched instead.

bindings.label: Kimi K3
bindings.why: The strongest measured column in the corpus, matching the catalogue entry's 'the hardest work, price no object'.
